newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close mixed, long bonds end weaker.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close mixed, long bonds end weaker.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed on Monday, with long bonds dropping sharply and shorter-term issues firming, as investors took profits on Canada-U.S. spreads at the long end, dealers said.
"At the long end there was some profit taking I believe on the Canada-U.S. spread compression trade," said Michael Gregory, an economist and strategist with with Lehman Brothers in Toronto.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.55 to C$115.10 to yield 6.767 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark fell 1/32 to yield 6.46 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 31 basis points from 27 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

The Canada-U.S. 30-year long bond spread has dropped sharply in the past month prompted by increasing investor recognition of Canada's positive bond market fundamentals. The spread reached an 11-year low of 20 basis points on November 6.
Analysts said some of today's profit taking may have been prompted by a weaker currency and an article in Barrons newspaper which drew attention to the prospects for the Canada-U.S. 30-year spread.
Investors are now looking ahead to the release tomorrow of Canada's consumer price index for October. Economists surveyed by Reuters forecast that core CPI will rise 1.3 percent year-over-year.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.08 to C$106.28 to yield 6.151 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.20 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was five basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.91 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.16 percent.
